inputs: issue #2129 body and maintainer reply (github.com page, fetched 2026-11-14)

refusals.what: Whether a new unsealed public attribute with a settable SurrogateType property belongs in the shipped MessagePack.Annotations assembly in this shape.
refusals.why_ai_cannot_decide: Public API shape, naming and the choice of a surrogate type are compatibility decisions that outlive this PR. No test can say whether the maintainers want to carry this surface.
refusals.question_for_owner: Do you accept GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute, as declared, as public API of MessagePack.Annotations?
options: Require sealed attribute and init-only property

refusals.what: Whether contractless mode may write every public read-write member of an external type by default.
refusals.why_ai_cannot_decide: The probe shows the generated bytes equal the built-in ContractlessStandardResolver, including a member marked [IgnoreDataMember] (Secret). Whether that exposure is acceptable for types the formatter's owner did not write is a data-exposure decision.
refusals.question_for_owner: Should the default require an opt-in list of members, or is 'all public read-write members' the contract you want to promise?
options: Require a surrogate for any type with sensitive members
Add a diagnostic when [IgnoreDataMember] members are written
refusals.resolvable_by: partly by evidence: runs/2129/probe/DataMemberAttributes.txt shows the behaviour, the policy stays human

citations.quote: By default the formatter serializes the type in *contractless* mode

refusals.what: Whether members that are read-only or have a non-public setter may be dropped from the wire format without any diagnostic.
refusals.why_ai_cannot_decide: A dropped member leaves no trace, and the agent's own test locks the omission of Doubled in. The probe confirms Name{get;} and PrivSet{get;private set;} are absent from the output. Whether a round trip that loses data should compile silently is a product decision.
refusals.question_for_owner: Do you accept silent omission, or must the generator report each skipped public member?
options: Require an analyzer warning per skipped public member
Require an opt-in attribute for read-only members
refusals.resolvable_by: partly by evidence: runs/2129/probe/ReadOnlyAndPrivateSetters.txt; the severity decision is human

citations.quote: Read-only members are skipped because they cannot be deserialized.

refusals.what: Whether 'attributes on the type are used if present', from the maintainer's reply on the issue, is part of this requirement.
refusals.why_ai_cannot_decide: The reply says attributes win when present, the issue's own motivation is a type that has none, and the agent implemented only the no-attribute path plus a surrogate. Which reading the requirement owner intended is not in the diff. The probe adds that [IgnoreMember] on T's own member is also written (runs/2129/probe/G1_IgnoreMemberOnFormattedType.txt).
refusals.question_for_owner: Is ignoring attributes that sit on T (for example [MessagePackObject] or [DataContract] on an in-assembly type) acceptable for this release?

citations.quote: members = CreateSurrogateMembers(type, surrogate, referenceSymbols, reportDiagnostic, location, out isIntKey);

refusals.what: Whether a second formatter for the same type, or a formatter for a type that already has [MessagePackObject], may silently get no generated body.
refusals.why_ai_cannot_decide: The probe builds two partial formatters for one type and one formatter for a [MessagePackObject] type. In both cases the extra formatter gets no members and the compiler reports CS0535, not a MsgPack diagnostic. No test in the change covers duplicates, so the README's 'nothing else needed' has no evidence behind it for this case.
refusals.question_for_owner: Should duplicate or conflicting formatter requests produce a MsgPack diagnostic that names the conflict?
refusals.resolvable_by: partly by evidence: runs/2129/probe/probe-dup.log; the diagnostic policy is human

refusals.what: Whether attributes other than [Key] and [IgnoreMember] on a surrogate member may be ignored without a diagnostic.
refusals.why_ai_cannot_decide: The probe puts [MessagePackFormatter(typeof(GemDoubleIntFormatter))] on a surrogate member and the wire shows [21], not [42]: the custom formatter is dropped and nothing reports it. The README only promises Key and IgnoreMember, so the behaviour is documented by omission. Whether silent ignoring is acceptable for an attribute the library itself defines is a product decision.
refusals.question_for_owner: Should an unsupported attribute on a surrogate member produce a diagnostic, or be honoured?
options: Require a diagnostic for unsupported attributes
refusals.resolvable_by: partly by evidence: runs/2129/probe/G3_CustomFormatterOnSurrogateMember.txt; the policy is human
